summary: Implemented net/retry.py retry(operation, attempts, clock=None) following docs/DECISIONS.md D-1..D-4: injected Clock, net.backoff.delays() schedule, only TransientError retried, attempts counts total calls, last error re-raised unchanged. Added 8 tests; the full suite passes (9 tests).
assumptions: docs/DECISIONS.md (referenced by net/retry.py) is the authoritative contract and takes precedence over the issue's wording 'retry on any exception' and 'using time.sleep'. Retrying all exceptions would violate D-3, and calling time.sleep directly would violate D-1. Production still sleeps for real through the default SystemClock, which calls time.sleep.
'Exponential backoff' means the project's shared schedule net.backoff.delays() (0.1s doubling, capped at 5s), per D-2.
No sleep happens after the final failed attempt; attempts < 1 raises ValueError (D-4).
questions_for_requester: Issue #41 asks to retry on any exception, but project decision D-3 retries only TransientError. Does the pricing-service client raise (or map its timeouts/5xx to) net.errors.TransientError? If not, retry() will not help those calls until the client maps them. Do you intend to override D-3 (e.g. via a configurable set of retryable exceptions)?
Do you want the backoff schedule for pricing calls to differ from the shared net.backoff.delays() defaults?
